name: Banh gia Cho Giong
summary: Bánh giá Chợ Giồng is a Gò Công Tây cake, also called bánh vá. The Tiền Giang provincial portal mills rice and mung bean. Tuổi Trẻ mills rice and soy, three parts to one. Both ingredient lists stay.
origin: Chợ Giồng, Gò Công Tây. Tuổi Trẻ says Chợ Giồng is the old name of chợ Vĩnh Bình.
culture: Tuổi Trẻ prints two names. One account says bánh giá because the batter and the bean sprouts, or the mung bean, define it. Another says bánh vá because the batter goes into a ladle. The paper does not choose.
Tuổi Trẻ says the cake is both a snack and a cake for a formal meal, and quotes the line about a girl leaving and the Chợ Giồng cake staying.
howToEat: The provincial portal says to mill good rice and mung bean, mix the flour with egg, wheat flour, and seasonings, and, as the cake fries, add a little minced pork, shrimp, minced bean sprouts, and peanuts. The extract stops while the cake is still hot.

Tuổi Trẻ soaks three parts rice and one part soy overnight, then mills them. The filling is bean sprouts, pork, and pork liver, covered with more batter, with one or two shrimp and peanuts on top, fried in a ladle-like mold in boiling oil. Some cooks add egg and pork brain to the batter. Eat it with herbs and a fish sauce of garlic, chili, lime, and sugar.
Tuổi Trẻ also says the old shrimp was red tôm đất, and that smaller shrimp is used now. A price was not printed. The price is Check on arrival.
where: Chợ Giồng, now chợ Vĩnh Bình, in Gò Công Tây, on the Tuổi Trẻ account. It is not a Mỹ Tho stall. A house number was not printed. The address is Check on arrival.

seoDescription: Bánh giá at Chợ Giồng, Gò Công Tây. The provincial portal uses mung bean. Tuổi Trẻ uses soy flour. The price is Check on arrival.
